sections.heading: Data structures beyond key and value

claims.text: A Redis sorted set is a collection of unique members ordered by an associated score, kept sorted on every insert so that reading in order needs no further work.
Redis names leaderboards and sliding-window rate limiters as uses of sorted sets.
Cloudflare built its rate-limiting counters on a store that speaks the memcached protocol, using only GET, SET and INCR, an atomic increment.
Redis Cluster splits the key space into 16384 hash slots, and each master node handles a subset of them.
Redis Cluster replicates asynchronously, so a write acknowledged by a master can be lost if the master dies before the write reaches its replicas.
When a master fails, one of its replicas wins an election and promotes itself to master.

recall.prompt: Which three operations did Cloudflare have available for its counters?

answer.text: GET, SET and INCR, the last being an atomic increment.

recall.prompt: Can a write acknowledged by Redis Cluster be lost? How?

answer.text: Yes. Replication is asynchronous, so the master can die before the write reaches a replica.
